provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Good manners at the table
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list two table manners.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper handwashing.

Introduction:
We eat food every day. Today we learn good manners at the table.

Content:
Wash hands with soap before eating. Use your right hand to eat. Chew with your mouth closed. Do not talk with food in your mouth. Use spoon and fork properly.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to eat. Show me how to wash hands. Show me chewing with mouth closed.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do before eating? How do we chew properly? Why should we not talk with food in mouth?

Summary:
Good table manners make eating nice for everyone.

topics.title: Helping at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name two ways to help at home.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate picking up toys.

Introduction:
Our homes need care. We can help our parents at home.

Content:
Pick up your toys after playing. Arrange your books neatly. Run small errands for mummy. Help set the table for meals. Keep your room tidy.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to pick up toys. Let us pretend to carry plates to the table.

Evaluation questions:
What toys can you pick up? How can you help mummy? Why is helping good?

Summary:
Helping at home makes our homes happy places.

topics.title: Helping in class
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify two ways to help in class.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate watering a plant.

Introduction:
Our classroom is like our second home. We can help our teachers and friends.

Content:
Share the books with friends. Water the class plant daily. Arrange the chairs neatly. Help clean the blackboard. Pick up papers on the floor.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to water the plant. Let us arrange chairs in a line.

Evaluation questions:
How do we share books? What does the plant need? Why do we help in class?

Summary:
Helping in class makes learning fun for everyone.

topics.title: Respecting elders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list two ways to show respect to elders.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate greeting elders properly.

Introduction:
Elders are older than us. We must show them respect.

Content:
Greet elders with good morning. Listen when elders talk. Do not interrupt when elders speak. Use please and thank you. Help elders carry heavy things.

Class activity:
Let us practice greeting elders. Let us pretend to listen to our principal.

Evaluation questions:
How do we greet elders? What do we do when elders talk? Why is respect important?

Summary:
Respecting elders shows we are good children.

topics.title: Making friends
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state two ways to make friends.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate playing kindly with others.

Introduction:
Friends make us happy. Today we learn how to make new friends.

Content:
Say your name to a new friend. Smile when you meet someone new. Play together with toys. Share your snacks with friends. Be kind to everyone.

Class activity:
Let us practice saying our names. Let us pretend to share toys with friends.

Evaluation questions:
What do we say to a new friend? How do we share toys? Why are friends important?

Summary:
Good friends make school a happy place.

topics.title: Kind hands and kind words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify kind hands and kind words.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate using kind words.

Introduction:
Our hands and words can hurt or help others. We must use them kindly.

Content:
Hands are not for hitting. Use hands to help and share. Use kind words like please and thank you. Do not call friends bad names. Say sorry when you hurt someone.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to help a friend. Let us practice saying please and thank you.

Evaluation questions:
What should hands not do? What are kind words? How do we say sorry?

Summary:
Kind hands and words make everyone happy.

topics.title: My school and my home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their school name.
The pupils should be able to say their address with help.

Introduction:
We have two important places-home and school. We must know them well.

Content:
Know your school name. Say your school name loudly. Know your house number. Know your street name. Know your area name. Say your address with help from adults.

Class activity:
Let us say our school name together. Let us practice saying our addresses.

Evaluation questions:
What is your school name? What is your house number? Why do we need to know our address?

Summary:
Knowing where we live and learn is very important.

topics.title: Safe people
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify safe people.
The pupils should be able to state what to do with strangers.

Introduction:
Some people can help us if we are in trouble. We must know who they are.

Content:
Police officers are safe people. Teachers are safe people. Your parents are safe people. Never follow strangers. Run to safe people if you feel scared.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to run to a teacher. Let us practice saying no to strangers.

Evaluation questions:
Who are safe people? What do you do with strangers? Why should we not follow strangers?

Summary:
Safe people help us stay safe always.

topics.title: Teamwork
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate working in a team.
The pupils should be able to list two benefits of teamwork.

Introduction:
Working together makes hard things easy. Today we learn about teamwork.

Content:
Build one tower together with friends. Clean up the classroom together. Share toys when playing. Help each other with tasks. Cheer for your team members.

Class activity:
Let us build a tower together. Let us clean the classroom together.

Evaluation questions:
How do we build together? Why do we share toys? What happens when we help each other?

Summary:
Teamwork makes work fun and easy.

topics.title: Revision and drama
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate good manners through drama.
The pupils should be able to sing the good manners song.

Introduction:
Today we practice all we have learned this term. We will use drama and songs.

Content:
Act out helping at home. Act out respecting elders. Act out making friends. Sing the good manners song. Remember all our lessons from this term.

Class activity:
Let us act out helping mummy. Let us sing the good manners song together.

Evaluation questions:
What did you learn this term? How do we show good manners? Why are songs good for learning?

Summary:
We have learned many good habits to make us better children.
